messages.subject: Creating mesh for huge dataset
parts:
Morning,

I've got a dataset with about 26,000 points, comprising 19,500 observations and the rest NA values where I wish to make predictions.

The inla.mesh.2D function seems to freeze the program whatever values I put in -- I suspect because it's triangulating this monster dataset. How can I rationally choose the parameters for inla.mesh.2D?


> range(x); range(y)
[1] 608666.4 635844.8
[1] 234133.0 275371.1

> dim(data)
[1] 26119    17

> bnd<-inla.nonconvex.hull(coords, convex=-0.1)

> mesh<-inla.mesh.2d(boundary=bnd, offset=c(.06,.1), max.edge=c(.05,.2))

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: Re: Creating mesh for huge dataset
parts: Nevermind, think I figured it out -- this coordinate system is in meters and with those offset / edge values (I'd used for a decimal degree system) I was making the triangles way to small.
